images.author: Cristian Samper
images.why: Clearly identified forest elephant at Dzanga Bai, with its body visible in a muddy rainforest clearing. Strong single-animal composition; native dimensions unverified.

images.author: Jerome Starkey
images.why: Caption explicitly identifies a large male forest elephant at Dzanga Bai with exceptionally long downward tusks. Excellent subject match; linked 1024px size falls below the preferred resolution.

images.author: Thomas Nicolon
images.why: Caption-confirmed forest elephant drinking mineral-rich water in Dzanga-Sangha. Solitary subject and atmospheric clearing make a strong poster option; native dimensions unverified.

images.author: Christiaan van der Hoeven / WWF-Netherlands
images.why: Caption identifies a forest elephant emerging into a clearing in Gabon. Rich green rainforest backdrop and visible downward tusks; native dimensions unverified.

images.author: Bruce Davidson / naturepl.com / WWF
images.why: Caption explicitly identifies African forest elephant mother and calf at Dzanga Bai. Clear bodies and authentic mineral-pool habitat; mother-and-calf composition rather than a lone male.

images.author: Thomas Nicolon
images.why: Caption confirms two male forest elephants playing in rain at Dzanga Bai. Strong behavioral alternative, although retaining both animals makes a 9:10 crop harder.

images.author: Coke Smith
images.why: Species-specific Loxodonta cyclotis gallery documents this Dzanga Bai photograph. Visible bodies, straight tusks and earthy colors; group framing requires careful cropping. Native resolution unverified.

images.author: Matthew Luizza/USFWS
images.why: Officially identified African forest elephants at Dzanga Bai; verified 4608 × 3456 original. Strong freely reusable habitat alternative, with a wider group composition.

images.author: Marijn van der Marel
images.why: Large standing common hippo photographed in Nyerere National Park, Tanzania. Strong land-based candidate with a clearly documented wild location; native dimensions unverified.

images.author: Alex Kraft
images.why: Wild common hippo grazing in Murchison Falls National Park, Uganda. Broad body visible against lush vegetation; grass partly obscures the feet.

images.author: Linda
images.why: Lakeshore grazing hippo photographed in Tanzania's Arusha Region. Source lists a 4912 × 3264 camera photograph; useful full-body habitat option.

images.author: Charlie Summers
images.why: Caption explicitly identifies a Hippopotamus amphibius bull charging into the South Luangwa River, Zambia. Excellent male/action match; linked 1024px size is below the preferred resolution.

images.author: Colin Watts
images.why: Common hippo family at a lakeshore in South Africa, identified by the photographer. Standing animals provide more body visibility; group composition needs a selective crop.

images.author: Bob Brewer
images.why: Yawning common hippo photographed in Ruaha National Park, Tanzania. Open-mouth alternative with strong facial impact; body partly submerged.

images.author: Michael Starkie
images.why: Camera photograph of an open-mouthed common hippo in Tanzania, identified in the caption and safari tags. Strong mouth-and-teeth emphasis; not a whole-body land view.

images.author: Jonathan Göhner
images.why: Captioned warning display, with Uganda and River Nile location tags. Large open jaws and visible tusks suit a tight 9:10 card; lower body submerged.
